subject: Discovery Recap: Structured Actions & Function Calls for PayFlux

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today

Alex / Priya — thanks again for a great conversation earlier. As promised, below is a short recap of the pains you described, the measurable goals we heard, and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned. Please correct anything I missed.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent structured outputs from your current LLM pipeline (missing keys, extra properties) — causes downstream payment reconciliation failures.
- Tight latency window for webhook-driven workflows: p95 target ~200ms.
- Audit & traceability requirements: need full request/response logs retained for 90 days and per-tenant access controls.
- Cost pressure at scale — 200–400k tokens/day expected in steady state.

Current stack (as described):
- Orchestration: internal node.js service behind API gateway
- Model layer: vendor-hosted GPT-4 variant via third-party provider for all generation and light post-processing
- Post-processing: brittle regex + heuristics to convert text -> JSON schema

Success criteria you called out (must-haves for POC acceptance):
1) Deterministic JSON outputs that validate against the canonical schema with >= 98% pass rate on your eval set.
2) P95 latency for end-to-end call (Redwood runtime + network) under 200ms for the a typical 100-token response.
3) Auditability: request/response logs available with tenant tags and immutable storage for 90 days.
4) Cost: projected per-token cost reduction vs current vendor by at least 20% at projected volumes.

What we propose for a short POC:
- 2-week technical POC using a representative prompt set (you’ll share ~500 examples).
- We’ll provide a schema-first approach (JSON Schema + function/agent wiring) and a small sandbox deployment in our dedicated environment.
- Evaluation plan: automated validator run on your examples + manual review of edge cases.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you share the 500 example prompts + expected JSON outputs by EOD Friday? (Priya)
- We’ll circulate a draft JSON schema and a sample function-call contract for your engineers to review (Marissa will send).
- Agree a POC kickoff slot — propose Thurs 2/26 at 10:00am PT for a 30-min technical kickoff.

Attachments: we’ll follow with a sample schema and a POC plan doc (I’ve attached a short stack snapshot to this thread per your request).

Thanks — Rishi

Rishi Malhotra

Thanks Rishi — this looks correct and concise. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The examples we’ll provide will include both successful and known-bad cases (we want Redwood’s validation to be able to flag the bad ones).
- For latency, our 200ms p95 target is for a cold end-to-end call originating from our gateway; we understand there’s network variance — we mainly want consistency and an SLA path.
- On audit logs: we need tenant-level role-based access so ops can pull audits for a single merchant without exposing other tenants.

Two asks before the kickoff:

2) Any compliance evidence you can share (SOC2 type II report summary) would help accelerate procurement.

We’ll aim to get the example set to you by Friday EOD; Priya will coordinate. Kickoff time looks fine — confirm if you can do 10am PT on Thursday.

Alex

Subject: Draft: JSON schema + function-call contract for POC (first pass)

Alex / Priya — looping in the technical details here so your engineering team can react directly. I attached a small sample schema and an example of the function-call contract we typically use in POCs. Key notes below.

Attachment: redwood-json-schema-sample.json (JSON Schema + example responses)

Summary of approach:
- Schema-first generation: prompts + function call signature guarantee a typed output. We prefer using JSON Schema draft-07 for compatibility with most validators you likely already have.
- Function-calling pattern: we will surface a single function name (e.g., create_reconciliation_entry) with a strict parameter schema. If the model returns a string that doesn't match shape, our runtime will mark it as "schema_violation" and include the raw payload in the audit log for manual review.
- Deterministic formatting: to hit the >=98% pass rate you requested, we combine: templated prompts, constrained sampling (top-p small + temperature ~0.0), and a validation+repair pass. Repair logic includes minimal, auditable fixes (trim whitespace, coerce numeric strings) but will not invent new fields. All repairs are logged.

Proposed POC evaluation metrics (automated):
- Schema validation pass rate on your 500-example set (target >=98%).
- Mean time-to-validate (should be <20ms server-side on our runtime).
- Rate of repair-invocations (we’ll flag >5% as a risk).
- P95 end-to-end latency (Redwood runtime + 2 network hops) target <200ms.

Sample function contract (human-readable):
- function: create_reconciliation_entry
- parameters (JSON Schema): {"merchant_id": "string", "transaction_id": "string", "amount": "number", "currency": "string", "status": "enum: [settled, failed, pending]", "line_items": "array"}

Operations notes:
- Logging & retention: we will enable tenant-tagged logs and can export immutable copies for your compliance team.
- RBAC: we’ll demo the tenant-scoped audit retrieval during kickoff.

Next steps I’ll take by end of day: 
1) Upload the redwood-json-schema-sample.json to the shared Drive link.
2) Share a short runbook for the POC data transfer (S3 presigned or secure upload).
3) Draft a minimal acceptance checklist for the POC.

If this looks good, we’ll confirm the kickoff (Rishi -- can you send the calendar invite for Thu 10am PT?)

—Marissa
